# Thursday evenings at the repair café — whether to open a second night (captain review, 2026-02-02)

For: the café's coordinating group, who decide how the volunteers' time and the $6K grant are spent,
and who know the Saturday sessions well.

<!-- An invented document, written only to exercise pitch's memo converter, its deck fence and the
captain review's shape: every block the converter places appears below at least once. No
organisation, person or figure in it is real. -->

## The answer

Open a second session on **Thursday evenings** for 10 weeks, run by the Thursday crew of 5 fixers
and paid from the *$6K grant*: $2.4K of it. Saturdays turn 31 people away a month; a second night
is the cheapest way to see them. The `hall` is free on Thursdays until June.

## Where things stand

| Month | Saturday visits | Repairs finished |
| --- | ---: | :---: |
| November | 112 | 71 |
| December | 96 | 58 |
| January | 124 | 80 |

- 31 people were turned away in January: the queue closed at 13:00.
- 5 fixers said they could do Thursdays:
  - 3 of them repair lamps, radios and kettles,
  - 2 repair bikes.
- About 64 % of January's visits ended in a finished repair (80 of 124).

#### Where the figures come from

The visit counts are the door tally; the repairs are the fixers' own log, kept in the
[sign-in sheet](visits-2026-01.csv) and summarised at <https://example.com/repair-cafe/tally>.
Read more on the method at [the network's guide](https://example.com/repair-cafe/guide "a guide").

> "We left with the lamp still broken, and came back the next month."
> — a visitor's card, January

## The options

### A — Open Thursday evenings for 10 weeks

- **You get at the end:** 10 more sessions, and a count of who comes on a weekday evening.
- **It costs:** $2.4K of the grant: the hall at $240 a night for 10 nights, tea included.
- **It needs from you:** a yes by 9 February, and one of you at the first night.
- **The one risk:** the crew tires by week 6; we would see it in the sign-in sheet first.

### B — Run Saturdays two hours longer

- **You get at the end:** the same visitors, seen later in the day.
- **It costs:** $1.2K: the hall's longer booking.
- **It needs from you:** a word with the hall's committee.
- **The one risk:** the fixers who come on Saturdays already leave at 13:00.

### C — Keep one session and book visits ahead

- **You get at the end:** no queue, and fewer walk-ins.
- **It costs:** nothing in money; a booking form to look after.
- **It needs from you:** nothing.
- **The one risk:** the visitors who never book stop coming.

## The best three

Ranked by what the group cares about most: people seen, then the volunteers' time.

1. **A** — the only option that sees the 31 people a month.
2. **C** — free, but it trades the queue for fewer visits.
3. **B** — it asks the same people for more hours.

The first night, as planned:

```text
Thursday 18:00–21:00   two benches, one for lamps and radios, one for bikes
```

---

## Decisions

**Legend.** D<n> a decision for the group; answer under `➤ Answer:`, in your own words or a letter.

- **D1 — Open Thursday evenings for 10 weeks?** A second night, paid from the grant.
  - A — open them, from 19 February
  - B — run Saturdays longer instead

  Reversible: yes

  ➤ Recommended: A — it is the only option that sees the people turned away.

  ➤ Answer:

  > The hall's Thursday rate holds until June.
